'''Leonard Francis Lindoy''', {{post-nominals|country=AUS|size=100%|sep=,|AO|}} [[Australian Academy of Science|FAA]], (born 1937)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lindoy, Leonard Francis (1937–) |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/people/544995 |access-date=2024-01-21 |website=Trove}}</ref> is an Australian chemist with interests in [[macrocycle|macrocyclic chemistry]] and metallo-[[supramolecular chemistry]], and an [[Emeritus Professor]] of [[Inorganic Chemistry]] at the [[University of Sydney]] and [[James Cook University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.science.org.au/events/sats/sats2009/ecr_awards_lindoy.html|title=Australian Academy of Science - SATS 2009|work=[[Australian Academy of Science|science.org.au]]|accessdate=8 August 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091006013956/http://www.science.org.au/events/sats/sats2009/ecr_awards_lindoy.html|archive-date=2009-10-06|url-status=dead}}</ref>  He moved to the University of Sydney in 1996 to take up the departmental [[chair (academic)|chair]] in inorganic chemistry vacated by [[Hans Freeman]].

== Honours and recognition ==
Lindoy has been recognised for his professional achievements with Fellowships in the [[Royal Australian Chemical Institute]] (RACI), the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (RSC), the Royal Society of New South Wales (RSN) and in 1993, the [[Australian Academy of Science]] (FAA).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.science.org.au/fellows/fellowship-list.html#L |title=Australian Academy of Science - Fellowship List |work=[[Australian Academy of Science|science.org.au]] |accessdate=8 August 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006230332/http://science.org.au/fellows/fellowship-list.html |archivedate= 6 October 2011 }}</ref>
In 1995, Lindoy received both the H G Smith Memorial Medal<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.raci.org.au/site/1/common/HG2009%20Smith%20Award.pdf|title=H G Smith Memorial Award|work=[[Royal Australian Chemical Institute|raci.org.au]]|accessdate=8 August 2010}}{{Dead link|date=November 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.raci.org.au/page/Awards/Past-Award-Winners.htm#hgsmith |title=Past Award Winner - H G Smith Memorial Medal |work=[[Royal Australian Chemical Institute|raci.org.au]] |accessdate=8 August 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20100715004607/http://www.raci.org.au/page/Awards/Past-Award-Winners.htm |archivedate=15 July 2010 }}</ref> and the Burrows Award, the premier award of the Inorganic Chemistry Division of the RACI.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.raci.org.au/page/Divisions/Inorganic-Chemistry/Inorganic-Chemistry-Awards.htm |title=Inorganic Chemistry Awards |work=[[Royal Australian Chemical Institute|raci.org.au]] |accessdate=8 August 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20100804060334/http://www.raci.org.au/page/Divisions/Inorganic-Chemistry/Inorganic-Chemistry-Awards.htm |archivedate= 4 August 2010 }}</ref>  Lindoy's contributions were also recognised by the [[Government of Australia|Australian Government]] in 2001 with a [[Centenary Medal]] for "service to Australian society and science in inorganic chemistry".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1127968|title=LINDOY, Leonard Francis: Centenary Medal|work=itsanhonour.gov.au|accessdate= 8 August 2010}}</ref> In 2005, he was awarded an RACI Distinguished Fellowship<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.raci.org.au/site/1/common/Distinguished2009%20Fellowship.pdf|title=Distinguished Fellowship|work=[[Royal Australian Chemical Institute|raci.org.au]]|accessdate=8 August 2010}}{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.raci.org.au/page/Awards/Past-Award-Winners.htm#distinguishedfellowship |title=Past Award Winners - Distinguished Fellowship |work=[[Royal Australian Chemical Institute|raci.org.au]] |accessdate=8 August 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20100715004607/http://www.raci.org.au/page/Awards/Past-Award-Winners.htm |archivedate=15 July 2010 }}</ref> and he went on to receive the 2008 Leighton Memorial Medal<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.raci.org.au/page/Awards/Past-Award-Winners.htm#leighton |title=Past Award Winners - Leighton Memorial Medal |work=[[Royal Australian Chemical Institute|raci.org.au]] |accessdate=8 August 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20100715004607/http://www.raci.org.au/page/Awards/Past-Award-Winners.htm |archivedate=15 July 2010 }}</ref> which is "the RACI's most prestigious medal and is awarded in recognition of eminent services to chemistry in Australia in the broadest sense."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.raci.org.au/site/1/common/Leighton2009%20Medal.pdf|title=Leighton Medal|work=[[Royal Australian Chemical Institute|raci.org.au]]|accessdate=8 August 2010}}{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>  In 2009, he received both the Australian Academy of Science's Craig Medal<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.science.org.au/awards/awardees/2009awards.html|title=2009 Awards|work=[[Australian Academy of Science|science.org.au]]|accessdate=8 August 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131209050339/http://www.science.org.au/awards/awardees/2009awards.html|archive-date=2013-12-09|url-status=dead}}</ref> and a [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (RSC) Centenary Lectureship and Medal.

Lindoy was appointed an [[Order of Australia|Officer of the Order of Australia]] in the [[2025 King's Birthday Honours (Australia)|2025 King's Birthday Honours]] for "distinguished service to chemical sciences as a researcher, to tertiary education, and in leadership roles".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Emeritus Professor Leonard Francis LINDOY |url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/3053738 |access-date=2025-06-11 |website=Australian Honours Search Facility}}</ref>
